title: Emergency Aid for Returning Americans Affected by Coronavirus Act
official_summary:
Emergency Aid for Returning Americans Affected by Coronavirus Act

This bill increases the maximum amount of funding available in FY2020 for, and revises certain requirements pertaining to, temporary assistance for U.S. citizens and their dependents who are returning from foreign countries due to a crisis and are without available resources. Under current law, the Department of Health and Human Services may provide assistance such as money payments and medical care to these individuals on a temporary basis.

In providing temporary assistance during the COVID-19 (i.e., coronavirus disease 2019) emergency declared on January 31, 2020, only certain members of the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service shall have direct, in-person contact with those receiving assistance. Specifically, they must be uniformed, active-duty members of the Regular Reserve Corps or the Ready Reserve Corps. In addition, they must have received training on infection prevention and control and have access to personal protective equipment.

summary.headline: This law raises the funding limit for temporary aid to returning U.S. citizens during 2020 and sets rules for which health staff may work directly with them during the COVID-19 emergency.
summary.what_it_does: The Department of Health and Human Services can give temporary help, such as money payments and medical care, to U.S. citizens and their dependents who return from foreign countries because of a crisis and have no resources. This law increases the maximum amount of funding for that help in fiscal year 2020. During the COVID-19 emergency, only certain Public Health Service Commissioned Corps members may have in-person contact with people receiving this aid. Those members must be uniformed, active-duty officers in the Regular Reserve Corps or Ready Reserve Corps, must be trained in infection prevention and control, and must have personal protective equipment.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. citizens and their dependents returning from foreign countries without available resources
who_it_affects.how: They may receive temporary money payments and medical care, and the total funding available for this help in fiscal year 2020 is higher.

who_it_affects.group: Active-duty Regular Reserve and Ready Reserve members of the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps
who_it_affects.how: They are the only members allowed to have direct, in-person contact with people receiving this aid during the COVID-19 emergency, and they must have infection-control training and protective equipment.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted July 13, 2020; the official summary does not list separate effective dates for each provision.
